name: Nose Shadow
description: Analyzes nose shadow casting patterns to detect synthetic artifacts, anomalies, and characteristic signatures of generative AI models.
mechanism:
This method analyzes nose shadow patterns for deepfake detection:

1. **Nose Shadow Detection**: The shadow cast by the nose (primarily on the cheek and upper lip) is detected per frame using luminance gradient analysis. The shadow's shape, direction, and intensity are measured.

2. **Shadow-Lighting Consistency**: The nose shadow direction should be consistent with the overall scene illumination. The method estimates the light source direction from the nose shadow and cross-validates against other facial shadows (orbital shadows, chin shadow, nasolabial shadows). Inconsistent shadow directions indicate manipulated lighting in the generated face.

3. **Shadow Shape Analysis**: The nose shadow shape should be geometrically consistent with the nose's 3D shape and the light direction. A straight nose bridge casts a different shadow than a curved one. The method checks whether the shadow shape is physically plausible given the detected nose geometry. AI generators may produce shadows that don't correspond to the nose geometry.

4. **Shadow-Pose Dynamics**: As the head rotates, the nose shadow should shift according to the changing angle between the nose and light source. The method tracks shadow position relative to nose landmarks across frames. In deepfakes, shadows may not respond correctly to head rotation — remaining static or moving independently of head pose.

5. **Soft Shadow Rendering**: Natural nose shadows show penumbra (soft edges) whose width depends on the light source size. The method evaluates shadow edge quality — AI generators may produce shadows with incorrect penumbra (too sharp or too soft) or no penumbra gradient, lacking the physical light-shadow relationship.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through nose shadow analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
Verdoliva, L. (2020). Media Forensics and DeepFakes: An Overview. IEEE JSTSP.
